governance_note: Descriptive business analysis only. No predictive model trained and no modeling target selected/ranked (G1).

insights.question: Which contact channel (cellular vs telephone) is associated with a higher term-deposit response rate?
insights.interpretation: Cellular contacts convert at ~14.7% versus ~5.2% for telephone - a 2.8x lift on the same population. Channel is a decisive, directly controllable factor.
insights.business_relevance: Conversion per outbound contact is the core efficiency of the campaign; a 2.8x channel gap is immediate upside without new client acquisition cost.
insights.recommended_action: Shift outbound capacity toward cellular where the same client can be reached either way, and treat telephone as a fallback channel.

insights.question: How do macroeconomic conditions relate to the response rate?
insights.interpretation: Response is strongly and inversely related to the interest-rate and labor-market environment: low euribor windows convert at 24-45% while high-rate windows sit at ~4.8%. The macro indicators are the strongest descriptive drivers.
insights.business_relevance: Timing and sizing campaigns to favorable economic windows changes booked deposits per call dramatically - potentially the largest lever available.
insights.recommended_action: Concentrate pushy/high-volume waves in low-rate windows and run minimal maintenance effort in high-rate windows; feed the macro indicators into the predictive model.

insights.question: Which customer demographic segments respond best?
insights.interpretation: Several segments are 2-4x the 11.27% base rate: students (31.4%) and retirees (25.2%) by job, and the 65+ (46.9%) and under-25 (21.0%) bands by age. Middle-aged salaried segments underperform.
insights.business_relevance: Curating calling lists toward high-propensity segments raises conversion per agent-hour at no additional spend.
insights.recommended_action: Prioritize retirees, students, and the 65+/under-25 age bands in targeting while still modeling these jointly with the macro context.

insights.question: How does prior contact history relate to response?
insights.interpretation: Warm history dominates: previously-contacted clients convert at ~64% versus ~9% for never-contacted, and poutcome='success' at ~65%. Yet 96% of rows are never-contacted cold leads, so the reachable-warm pool is small but extremely high value.
insights.business_relevance: Focusing re-contact budgets on warm leads is the single highest-yield targeting rule; the huge cold share means a good model is still needed to find the ~11% who convert cold.
insights.recommended_action: Guarantee warm/previously-contacted leads are worked first. Use history features in the model, but review poutcome for decision-time availability before production use (leakage flag).

insights.question: How does contact intensity relate to conversion and outbound effort?
insights.interpretation: Marginal conversion declines with more attempts (13.0% on the first down to ~5.5% at 6+), while 83% of total contact volume is spent on repeat attempts, averaging ~23 contacts per subscriber under current policy.
insights.business_relevance: Effort is heavily consumed by low-yield repeat dialing; capping attempts and reallocating to higher-propensity targets improves campaign margin.
insights.recommended_action: Introduce attempt caps tied to predicted propensity and redirect saved capacity to high-probability cold leads identified by the model.

cross_insight_summary: The dominant, mutually consistent story: response is driven primarily by WHEN the market is favorable (macro/rate environment, Q02) and WHO has warm history (Q04), then by channel (Q01) and segment (Q03), while current effort is inefficiently spread across repeat contacts (Q05). A propensity model plus band-based outreach rules can reallocate a fixed calling budget toward high-probability contacts.
